items.informal_name: Compatibility of Evaluation and Variable Substitution in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} {S : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] (f : τ → S) (g : σ → MvPolynomial τ R) (φ : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.aeval f) ((MvPolynomial.bind₁ g) φ) = (MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => (MvPolynomial.aeval f) (g i)) φ
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \tau $, and an $ R $-algebra $ S $, given a variable assignment $ f : \tau \to S $ and a substitution map $ g : \sigma \to R[\tau] $, the evaluation of a polynomial $ \varphi \in R[\sigma] $ after substituting variables via $ g $ and then applying algebra evaluation $ \text{aeval}_f $ is equal to evaluating $ \varphi $ with each variable $ i \in \sigma $ replaced by $ \text{aeval}_f(g(i)) $. Formally, $ \text{aeval}_f(\text{bind}_1(g, \varphi)) = \text{aeval}_{(i \mapsto \text{aeval}_f(g(i)))}(\varphi) $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Evaluation and Variable Substitution in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} {S : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] (f : τ → S) (g : σ → MvPolynomial τ R),
  (MvPolynomial.aeval f).comp (MvPolynomial.bind₁ g) = MvPolynomial.aeval fun i => (MvPolynomial.aeval f) (g i)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, and $ R $-algebra $ S $, given a variable assignment $ f : \tau \to S $ and a substitution map $ g : \sigma \to R[\tau] $, the composition of the algebra evaluation homomorphism $ \text{aeval}(f) $ with the variable substitution homomorphism $ \text{bind}_1(g) $ equals the algebra evaluation homomorphism obtained by first substituting variables via $ g $ and then evaluating using $ f $. Formally, $ (\text{aeval}\, f) \circ (\text{bind}_1\, g) = \text{aeval}(i \mapsto \text{aeval}\, f(g(i))) $.

items.informal_name: Composition Identity for Multivariate Polynomial Evaluations
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {S : Type u_2} {τ : Type u_3} {x : τ → S}
  [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] (f : R →+* MvPolynomial τ S) (g : σ → MvPolynomial τ S) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.eval x) (MvPolynomial.eval₂ f g p) =
    MvPolynomial.eval₂ ((MvPolynomial.eval x).comp f) (fun s => (MvPolynomial.eval x) (g s)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ S $, type $ \tau $, and evaluation map $ x : \tau \to S $, evaluating a multivariate polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $ first with coefficient map $ f : R \to S[\tau] $ and variable map $ g : \sigma \to S[\tau] $, then evaluating the result at $ x $, is equivalent to directly evaluating $ p $ using the composed coefficient map $ \text{eval}_x \circ f $ and variable map $ s \mapsto \text{eval}_x(g(s)) $. This equality holds for all $ p $ and establishes compatibility of evaluation homomorphisms with composition.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Composed Polynomials: $(p \circ q)(x) = p(q(x))$
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {p q : Polynomial R} {x : R},
  Polynomial.eval x (p.comp q) = Polynomial.eval (Polynomial.eval x q) p
items.informal_description: For polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ over a commutative semiring $ R $, and for any element $ x \in R $, the evaluation of the composition $ p \circ q $ at $ x $ equals the evaluation of $ p $ at $ q(x) $, i.e., $ (p \circ q)(x) = p(q(x)) $.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of Multivariate Polynomials Composes with Ring Homomorphisms
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S₁ : Type v} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S₁] (f : R →+* S₁)
  (g : σ → R) (p : MvPolynomial σ R), f ((MvPolynomial.eval g) p) = MvPolynomial.eval₂ f (⇑f ∘ g) p
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S_1 $, any map $ g : \sigma \to R $, and any polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, it holds that $ f(\mathrm{eval}_g(p)) = \mathrm{eval}_{f, f \circ g}(p) $, where $ \mathrm{eval}_g $ denotes evaluation using variable map $ g $ and identity coefficient map, and $ \mathrm{eval}_{f, f \circ g} $ denotes evaluation using coefficient map $ f $ and variable map $ f \circ g $.
